chapters.title: Chapter 452 What the fuck is this?
paragraphs: The entire inn where Qingyi was staying was silent.
The candles, torches, and mana crystals that illuminated it had been extinguished, leaving nothing but the moonlight streaming through the glass windows to light it.
In the center of the main hall, there was a single table. At it, a cloaked figure rested his back against the wooden chair.
His fingers, calloused from years of wielding swords, reached for a cup of tea on the table. His lips parted, accepting a single sip into himself.
"Ah..." The man lifted his noble, aged face, staring at the figure slowly descending the stairs.
"I don't believe you're here for good reasons." The figure's voice echoed: masculine, dignified, and soft, strangely pleasant to the ears.
It was Long Qingyi. As for the man waiting for him, he already had an idea of who he was.
"You hurt my son quite a bit..." The man spoke, confirming Qingyi's suspicions.
That man was a count, the father of the nobleman whose hand he had broken and whose subordinate he had killed a few days ago.
"I gave him nothing more than what he was looking for," Qingyi said.
The Lord did not answer him immediately, pouring some tea for Qingyi.
"Drink, it's not-"
Before the lord could even finish his sentence, Qingyi had already taken a sip of tea.
"...poisoned..."
"It's sweet... don't you have anything stronger?" Qingyi asked, placing the teacup back on the table.
Even if it was poisoned, he highly doubted that this man possessed a poison capable of affecting him.

The lord paused for a brief moment before bursting into laughter. "HAHAHAHAHA, you are a very... very interesting man, hahahaha..." The lord slammed his hand on the table, pulling out a bottle of wine, one of the highest quality in his collection and which, fortunately, by a stroke of fate, he had decided to bring with him that day.
The moment he opened it, a strong smell of wine filled the room, capable of bewitching even a True Immortal.
Qingyi watched the blood-red liquid being poured into a glass, smelling it for a brief moment before taking a single sip.
"How is your son's hand? Honestly, I wanted to blow his balls off too, but I was in a hurry," Qingyi asked, placing the glass on the table.
"He's fine. A whiny, arrogant bastard, but he's still my son. He doesn't die from so little."
"I imagine," Qingyi replied, watching that man coldly.
He was a count, and a powerful one at that, whose power was equivalent to a peak True Immortal.
Yet he sat there casually, without any guards or restrictions, drinking casually alongside a man he had just met.
"I believe you are here on diplomatic business, correct? For an
Oriental to be so far from home."
"Not exactly," Qingyi shook his head. "It's not something I can tell you without having to cut out your tongue."
"Hm..." The lord scratched his chin. "Having my tongue is... pretty good."
He took a sip from his wine glass and then stood up.
"I have cut out the tongues of some men in the past. Some by my own desire, some by order of His Imperial Majesty, and others by the wishes of the Church."
"I believe you are one of these." The lord extended his hands toward Qingyi.
The moment the handsome young man held them, the lord smiled, whispering, "The winds in the North are cold... the Blood Lord awaits you in his eternal embrace."
As soon as that voice came out, Qingyi sensed danger. A demonic energy surged from the Lord's gut, like a spear of blood.
Qingyi spun his body as a powerful bloody spear surged forth, tearing toward him.
He barely managed to dodge.
The spear grazed his cheek, encountering nothing but the black
dragon's scales.
An explosion of sparks engulfed the hall, followed by a shockwave that immediately destroyed everything around them.
"A demonic cultist, huh?" Qingyi smiled, grabbing the spear and squeezing it. The steel, like crimson glass, shattered directly. "These parasites are really everywhere."
The lord's face changed completely. His calm blue eyes turned blood red, filled with a tremor and a slight surprise.
Had Qingyi dodged it?
No... what the hell were those black scales? His spear was barely able
to scratch them!
He tried to retreat, but naturally, Qingyi didn't allow it. His fist tore through the air at a terrifying speed, rising toward the demonic cultist's chin.
The cultist's face caved in, his nose was crushed, and his body was
thrown like a rag doll, so fast that he became nothing but a blur, breaking through the wooden walls and heading toward the skies. It took a whole second for the shockwave from that blow to spread,
the entire inn immediately turned to dust.
Fortunately, there was no one but Qingyi there.
"Damn... this brat is too strong! I should have chosen an easier
target... The cultist grunted, spinning in the air.
His face suddenly filled with terror as he called upon his demonic
energy. Two types of demonic energy, to be more specific.
The two formed two protective barriers around him, which, unfortunately, did little to stop Qingyi.
The handsome young man appeared in front of him, launching a downward kick.
Fortunately, they were no longer above the village, so Qingyi didn't
hold back.
The outer barrier held Qingyi's attack for a single moment before
collapsing.
The power sent the demonic cultist flying downward at supersonic speed, hitting the ground where the inner barrier collapsed, taking everything within a five-kilometer radius with it.
Blood rose to the demonic cultist's throat, and he opened his mouth, trying to bite the poison between his teeth and kill himself, but Qingyi obviously didn't allow it.
Teleporting in front of the cultist, Qingyi stuck his hand into the cultist's mouth, pulling out a tooth and the poison capsule, immediately sealing the cultist's cultivation.
At that moment, when he sealed that Qi, Qingyi realized something.
In the midst of the adrenaline rush, he hadn't even paid attention.
The lord used Mana, not Qi.
His first attack against Qingyi used Mana!
Qingyi immediately activated his draconic eyes, observing the man's
body.
There was a Mana heart in his chest and, just below it, a Dantian.
"What the fuck is this?"

chapters.title: Chapter 453 Do I need to repeat the question?
paragraphs: Qingyi crouched in front of the demonic cultist.
His beautiful purple eyes were cold as he watched him struggle desperately.
The damage to the man's body had been catastrophic. More than half of his bones were broken, his legs reduced to a mess, and his mouth was filled with blood.
Of course, that was far from enough to kill a True Immortal. But still, the pain was absurd.
"You're going to have to answer me a lot of questions..." Qingyi said.
He opened the system store and bought one of the highest quality healing pills available.
The cultist tried to resist, but Qingyi didn't care. He forced the man to open his mouth and shoved the pill down his throat.
"Ugh... son of a bitch..."
The cultist's words were cut off before they were even finished. A punch tore through the air at an absurd speed, broke his jaw, and sent him to the ground, just in time for the pill to take effect.
Even without actively circulating energy through the body, it was still a high-quality pill. On its own, it was almost enough to revive the dead.
Immediately, the cultist's wounds began to heal. A last gulp of blood left his lips as his broken jaw snapped back into place, his bones cracking painfully.
Even though he was a True Immortal thousands of years old, he couldn't stop the groans of agony, his red eyes widening.
That damn thing healed too fast without him being able to control it! "Ah... uff... uff..." The cultist gasped heavily, trying to get up.
He crossed his knees, pushed himself up, and then fell to the ground. He was exhausted.

"You know..." The cultist flashed a bloody smile, raising his hands. "We have a lot of assholes like you among us. I thought we could even be good friends... why don't we talk more amicably? A talented young man like you must be very ambitious, I can help you reach a level never seen before."
Qingyi did not respond.
He knew well how unorthodox cultivators operated.
There were those who were unorthodox by the nature of their cultivation. And there were those who, in addition to the nature of their cultivation, had rot in their souls.
They were snakes. No, worse than snakes.
They hid among orthodox cultivators like cockroaches; they lied and they manipulated.
He was sure that this cultist had maintained the identity of a pure and honorable noble for centuries, using it for the most terrible acts.
Qingyi was not a good person and would never convince himself otherwise. Still, compared to those corrupt pigs, he was an angel incarnate.
"You have a mana heart and a Dantian too. How is that possible?" Qingyi questioned, eliciting a laugh of contempt from the cultist.
"Ask my..."
The cultist's words were interrupted again.
But this time, it wasn't by a punch.
Qingyi pressed a single finger against one of the cultist's newly healed feet, moving his demonic Qi.
"ARGH! DAMN IT! Y-you... UGHN..."
The cultist writhed. His lips opened in a guttural scream that spread throughout the forest, stirring it for a brief moment.
The pain was horrible. The smell of burning flesh was accompanied by whitish smoke as Qingyi's lightning Qi destroyed everything it
touched.
Blood spurted onto the handsome young man's face, but he didn't
care.
"Do I need to repeat the question?"
Qingyi's lips lifted slightly. Blood slid down his cheeks, and his eyes were filled with a strange cold gentleness.
He didn't even seem to recognize that he was in the midst of torture, and this only terrified the cultist even more.
Unfortunately for the prisoner, he had taken too long to answer.
Qingyi's fingers flowed to the other foot, and then came the pain.
The terrible smell of burning flesh, smoke, and blood. Everything again, with the same intensity as before.
"I can make this much slower than it needs to be," Qingyi murmured, looking at the cultist, whose face was already drenched in tears.
It was... pathetic.
A being whose power rivaled that of a True Immortal, bearer of a mana heart and a Dantian, being reduced to tears so easily.
Qingyi still remembered many years ago, when he tortured the King of the Heavenly Thunder Kingdom, who had tried to take Ruxue from
him.
Even that Golden Core Realm cultivator endured the same torture
with much more dignity than this cultist. And that king was barely a fraction of what this man was.
Qingyi moved his hand toward the cultist's knee, who trembled.
"W-wait! I-I really can't talk! If I talk, the heartworm in my chest will
kill me immediately!"
He hoped that the excuse would work, that Qingyi would at least give
him a quick death.
Unfortunately, he didn't know Qingyi.
The handsome young man placed his hand on the cultist's chest and
used his spatial Qi.
In the next moment, the space between his fingers distorted. The
cultist's eyes filled with shock as he felt a weight lift from his heart, while at the same time a small red worm appeared in Qingyi's hands.
"Go ahead. Start talking." Qingyi crushed the worm.
The cultist gulped. His lips parted, but no words came out.
Only after a moment of hesitation did he finally begin:
"In the far west, there is a Dark Master, a powerful Qi user... He was
the one who initiated me. He helped me become a noble and gave me a Dantian! I don't know how the procedure works, I swear! I-I just fell asleep, and when I woke up, my body had completely changed."
"Hm..." Qingyi scratched his chin.
A Dark Master in the far west, with a connection to mana and Qi.
"Why did you attack me?" he asked.
He needed to know if the attack had occurred because he had already
been recognized as one of the Five Heroes.
If that was the case, things could get a little dangerous.
"D-debt... t-to pay off a debt! The master ordered us to capture as
many people as possible for a great sacrifice!"
"Hm..." Qingyi exhaled thoughtfully.
"P-please... no more, that's all I know... I-I'm telling the truth," the
cultist whimpered.
"I know you are."
Qingyi smiled. With a gentle movement of his hand, the cultist's head
flew through the air.

The pain of having every vein, every meridian, every inch of his dantian broken and rebuilt, was barely able to elicit a slight grunt
from him.
Still, his fingers trembled as he raised his hand, bringing it to the system screen, and then clicking to also improve his constitution and
lineage.
The pain multiplied tenfold in a single moment. Qingyi's vision darkened before suddenly lighting up even more brightly, his brain clearer than ever and his muscles, destroyed and torn, burning with
power.

In just a moment, the air around him heated up, enough to be able to melt steel like butter, even the black stones beginning to suffer. His skin cracked, expanding and retracting painfully, the reddish flesh visible, the cracks already soaking him in blood.
In his dantian and eyes, the strands of draconic Qi began to multiply,
needing only a moment to break through ten thousand, continuing to increase in quantity rapidly.
Qingyi just gritted his teeth, holding on tightly as time passed.
Only after nearly fifteen minutes was he finally able to let a relieved
sigh escape his lips.

level]

The scales, once so thin that they seemed like a second skin, were
now thick and powerful, clinging to his entire body like steel armor.
On his head, the small horns he had before had grown, and on his back, small trunks had appeared, almost like the base for wings to
emerge.
Even his claws had changed, much longer and sharper than before. Qingyi couldn't help but exhale in excitement.
It had been a long time since his black dragon scales had been upgraded, and many times he had encountered enemies powerful enough to damage them.
Although he rarely used them in combat, they were still important,
especially for defending against sneak attacks and, of course, suicidal
enemies.
With the current power of his black scales, he had no doubt that he would be able to survive a nuclear bomb.
"Not that there are many of those in this world, hahaha," Qingyi laughed before getting up and following his wives.

chapters.title: Chapter 462 - Prepare for death!
paragraphs: "Argh... damn it!" An angry grunt echoed as a blade cut through the dense forest, slowly clearing a path covered in weeds.
The owner of that voice was a young man with short golden hair and blue eyes. His cloak was torn, and even underneath, his silver armor was in pieces, covered in putrid, blackened blood.
He had taken a bad route, facing a ton of monsters, fighting countless battles, and sinking knee-deep in blood.
But fortunately, it was all over.
He had reached his destination, and now, it wouldn't be long before he could finally take a hot shower.
On the horizon, he could already see the path that led to the cabin, and the moment he stepped onto it, he quickened his pace.
When he finally arrived, he opened the door without hesitation.
He couldn't help but frown when he saw Qingyi there, especially when he saw who was next to him, lovingly feeding him.
Aeryn, the cold elven beauty. Her long, delicate fingers gripped a translucent cup as she carefully removed a spoonful of its contents and placed it in Qingyi's mouth.
The handsome young man simply accepted the spoon, eating calmly.
Lucien struggled to wipe the frown from his face, controlling his breathing, his body locking up uncontrollably.
'Since when had these two become so close?' Lucien thought before looking away.
This was not the time to dwell on such things; he had something bigger in front of him.
"Brother Qingyi." Lucien bowed. "I see you are... well." His nose suddenly caught a scent, something already lost in his memories.
'Is that... pudding?' Lucien wondered, his eyes shining.
The smell was identical, even the consistency on the spoon the high elf brought to Qingyi's mouth was the same, but it couldn't be.
Pudding didn't exist in this world, he was sure of it.
"You look well too," Qingyi said, clearly ironically, his eyes focused on Lucien, who immediately went to one of the bathrooms.
"Yes, and I'll be even better after this shower," Lucien said, shaking his head and suppressing useless thoughts.
"When I get out, we need to start preparing for the invasion of that damn necromancer's lair. The longer we take, the more innocents he kills."
Qingyi just nodded and soon got up, stretching slightly.
His wives soon gathered around him, and when Lucien finally left the bathroom, refreshed, he took a huge map out of his space ring and placed it on a wooden table.
It was a rough map, showing the outlines of where they were within a radius of about a hundred kilometers.

At this very moment, they were on a large plain covered with forests and rivers; to the north, the terrain became more mountainous, marking the beginning of the path that led to the land of the dragon elves.
To the east was the City of Light Breeze, an isolated but wealthy settlement, especially due to the extraction of spiritual wood.
To the southwest, there was little more than a vast emptiness, with a single point marked in the middle.
"According to our scouts, that is the entrance to the necromancer's lair, or at least where most of the kidnapped were taken immediately after capture.
It must be full of traps, but nothing we can't handle. We just need to keep Celestia well protected."
Lucien looked up at Qingyi again, then at Celestia.
The beauty was barely paying attention to what Lucien was saying, totally focused on her husband, her eyes filled with an intense glow of affection.
That only made Lucien's heart sink even further.
He didn't know, and to be honest, the possibility that she already considered herself Qingyi's wife hadn't even crossed his mind.
He knew Qingyi was intelligent; no one that intelligent would try to take the holy priestess of the Church of Auranys.
And if they did, their death would be slow, painful, and horrible.
Lucien's eyes then turned to Aeryn and Sapphire, both paying a little more attention to his words, but ultimately totally focused on Qingyi.
How could he stop jealousy from taking over his heart?
He didn't know, he was tired and frustrated.
He just wanted to get rid of those demonic cultists as quickly as possible and then leave, back to his routine of training and prayers until he could finally fulfill his destined prophecy.
"And what do you plan to do to get in?" Qingyi asked, leaving the final decision to Lucien.
Like it or not, he was technically the leader of that group of heroes.
"We can send minor attacks little by little, test their defenses, and then allow them to continue torturing and killing countless innocents
before we finally intervene.
Or we can go there right now and crush them like the cockroaches they are," Lucien declared.
"Hm... I like the second plan better." Qingyi smiled.
Was it a stupid plan? Absolutely, but he didn't care.
He liked to be direct, just as he liked to crush ants, and in the end,
even Aeryn, who didn't like to be so direct, had to agree with that idea.

In the end, everyone just wanted to solve the problem as quickly as possible and then never set foot in that godforsaken place again. Besides, of course, the fact that they wanted to join their husband soon and no longer be bound by those damn doctrines.
The church would probably want to continue giving them orders after they completed those missions, and their organizations would probably make them obey those rules.

Well, it was a pity for these organizations and for the church as well. "Very well." Lucien stood up, and soon everyone began to prepare. Swords were sharpened, staffs prepared, and spells organized. Fortunately, they already had an idea of what the inside of that cave was like thanks to previous spies, so they were a little more relaxed.
The young hero was the first to leave, pushing all bitterness and jealousy from his heart, pretending that Qingyi didn't even exist as the five heroes tore through the skies.
When they got close to the entrance of the lair, he dove in, throwing a huge space-blocking talisman while swinging his sword.
"We've arrived, heretics! Prepare for death!"
Lucien's attack landed with a bang, tearing through the first cultists
standing in front of the lair's entrance.
The poor wretches barely had time to react.
Soon, the massacre would begin.

chapters.title: Chapter 463 - Demonic lair (01)
paragraphs: That lair was... different.
Usually, such refuges were almost impossible to find, incomparable networks of tunnels with hundreds of false entrances.
The real one always changed. One week it was in one place; the next, it was dozens or hundreds of kilometers away, always surrounded by cloaking arrays.
That lair was not like that.
The surrounding forest area was clear, and for dozens of kilometers, all the villages were burning. Even signs of recent battles with local purge forces were clearly visible.
It was strange, as if they knew what was about to happen and trusted that the church was preventing the empire from sending any specialist powerful enough to exterminate them in a single breath.
Both Sapphire and Aeryn had the same thought in mind, but in the end, they remained silent.
Celestia didn't care much about such things, and Qingyi hardly seemed to take it seriously, while Lucien himself was too busy with his impulsiveness and jealousy to notice anything around him.
The two beauties could only exchange cautious glances, staying close to Qingyi.

The entrance to the lair was simple: a hole in the ground with a greenish brick mausoleum on top. The only access door was guarded by two guards with power equivalent to a False Immortal realm cultivator.
They were no match for Lucien's attack. A blade of light and golden mana emerged from his sword, striking the entrance with a bang.
Before the bodies cut in half even hit the ground and the mausoleum began to collapse, hundreds of magic arrays and Qi arrays activated at the same time.
From defensive arrays, forming hundreds of barriers around them, to offensive arrays, with thousands of blades rising to the skies, immediately targeting them.
"Oh... it seems we have a little group of interesting mice here..."
A voice echoed, feminine and sensual. From where the thousands of blades had appeared, a woman came.
Just like the cultist Qingyi had killed before, she also had both a Dantian and a mana heart. Her voluptuous body rose to the skies, propelled by the two energies.
Qingyi barely paid attention to that woman's status screen before shuddering.
That thing with breasts must have so many STDs that, in his past life, she would have been classified as a biological weapon.
Perhaps not even his body, powerful and resistant to almost every kind of poison, would be able to prevent his dick from falling off if he got one step closer to any of that woman's holes.
"Who are you, heretic? Tell me your name!" Lucien demanded, pointing his sword at the woman.
Behind her, other figures appeared. Dozens, hundreds, thousands, quickly surrounding the group.
"These are..." Aeryn's eyes widened as she tried to recognize those
creatures.
"Jiangshi, a type of undead used by unorthodox cultivators in my land," Qingyi replied, watching the creatures with interest.
Their skin was dark, and between their rotten teeth, almost covered by the talismans on their foreheads, black blood flowed incessantly.
He had never seen one of these in person, although he had heard many stories.
From their robes, they were the soldiers sent on the many extermination missions, at least the most powerful among them.
Their red eyes were empty, and their limbs stretched out sickeningly. Among them, more figures appeared, this time similar to that woman, though a little weaker.
They were just False Immortals with a few True Immortals, compared to her, who was at the peak of the True Immortal realm.
"Oh..." The woman's eyes changed, focusing on Qingyi.
Her body turned into a blur, and in a single moment, she appeared in front of Qingyi.
"We have a very interesting one here, tell me your—"
The woman couldn't even finish her sentence as Qingyi's fist tore
through the air.
Intense pain overwhelmed her jaw, burning blood exploding as she was sent flying backward like a cannonball. Dust rose as a shockwave
spread out.
She only stabilized after nearly five hundred meters, her jaw hanging below her face, every bone reduced to dust.
What the hell had just happened? How could that bastard have such strength?
She only didn't grit her teeth because she was physically incapable of
doing so.
Using a sound transmission to order her subordinates to attack, her eyes burned with rage as her demonic Qi and mana burned.
In the skies, the thousands of flying blades changed, taking a single
moment before exploding into speed. Tearing through the air at supersonic speed, they carried with them enough power to kill a False
Immortal.
Individually, they weren't much, but together? They were extremely
dangerous.
Sapphire summoned a barrier that encapsulated both Celestia and Aeryn, but this protection wasn't even necessary.
Qingyi placed himself in front of them, the Heaven-Defying Thunder Sword cutting through the air, easily parrying the first blade.
The impact caused his feet to sink into the ground, his back hitting
the barrier behind him.
But he didn't care, continuing to swing his sword as thousands of blades converged on his figure.
The world seemed to slow down as he easily parried everything, calculating the trajectory with his draconic eyes.
Each swing of his sword caused him to be engulfed by powerful shockwaves, the ground beneath his feet being further destroyed.
"Bastard!"
The cultist advanced toward Qingyi, her broken jaw snapping back into place. A guttural, terrible scream escaped her cracked red lips, nothing but pure hatred taking over everything.
Her nails grew, sharp as razors, slashing toward Qingyi's neck.
The handsome young man simply covered his neck with black scales.
The impact of that woman's claws caused nothing but a sea of sparks and broken nails, barely leaving a scratch on Qingyi.
His eyes descended, full of contempt, watching the shock on the
woman's face.
"You're pretty persistent for a disgusting and annoying little worm,
huh?"
Without hesitation, Qingyi kicked.
This time, not sending her flying away; quite the opposite.
His feet made contact with her face, and then he smashed her into
the ground with all his strength, immediately turning everything beneath him to dust.

The impact of that woman's claws caused nothing but a sea of sparks and broken nails, barely leaving a scratch on Qingyi.
His eyes descended, full of contempt, watching the shock on the
woman's face.
"You're pretty persistent for a disgusting and annoying little worm,
huh?"
Without hesitation, Qingyi kicked.
This time, not sending her flying away; quite the opposite.
His feet made contact with her face, and then he smashed her into
the ground with all his strength, immediately turning everything beneath him to dust.

chapters.title: Chapter 464 - Demonic lair (02)
paragraphs: "Shit..." Sapphire growled, rising into the sky as the ground beneath her feet ceased to be solid.
Even Lucien couldn't help but be taken by surprise, his eyes widening in shock as everything below him disappeared.
Qingyi's blow created deep furrows in the earth and a crater that nearly swallowed the entrance to the mausoleum whole.
The defensive arrays collapsed and when the dust settled, Qingyi was more than twenty meters deep, his feet sinking into a bloody mess shaped like a woman's head.
Her body convulsed, her soul destroyed by Qingyi, as well as her brain and, of course, her beautiful face.
Qingyi simply withdrew his foot, rising into the air.
"Ugh... did you really have to do it in such a disgusting way?" Sapphire asked, looking away from the blood-covered young man.
"No." Qingyi shook his head. A slight smile spread across his lips as he stretched, watching the other cultists, who were in deadly silence.
Honestly, they were lucky.
If there had been even one Immortal Emperor there, they would have been exterminated in a single moment.
'That's not all...' Qingyi repeated to himself.
It was impossible that such a miserable level of power would be enough to worry the emperor and even the church.
"This must have something to do with this procedure of being able to support a mana heart and a Dantian at the same time,' Qingyi thought to himself, lifting his face.
"What are you waiting for? Let's slaughter these bastards!" Beside him, Lucien's roar echoed, his blade slashing dozens of golden cuts
toward the enemy.
Celestia knelt down, casting a small blessing on her allies, while Aeryn also moved, her body glowing gold, taken over by the aura of the priestess's blessings.
Sapphire, right behind them, simply raised her hands in the air, hundreds of ice spears appearing behind her before she hurled them toward the enemies.
Soon, all the demonic cultists were overcome by nothing but the deepest chaos.
The Jiangshi ran wildly toward their opponents, barely resisting for a single moment before being destroyed by the heroes' joint attacks.
Qingyi, naturally, did not stand idly by.
He eliminated any undead or cultists that came too close to Sapphire and Celestia, drenching the Heaven-Defying Thunder Sword in blood as he reaped one enemy after another.
Barely a minute of battle had passed before the cultists began to flee desperately. Unfortunately for them, Sapphire would not allow it.
She placed her hands on the ground, gritted her teeth, and then moved all her mana toward her palms while whispering in an ancient language.
Instantly, the world around her changed.
A powerful blue barrier surged from her body, expanding violently and encapsulating all the cultists before finally ceasing to grow and transforming into a physical barrier.
"Eliminate them quickly! I won't be able to hold them back for long!" Sapphire roared to her companions.
Qingyi just nodded, receiving a second blessing from Celestia, feeling his body become much lighter and his mind much clearer.
That was... very useful.
Without further hesitation, he just advanced, using his draconic eyes to detect all enemies and, in a single moment, exterminate them
completely.
When they were finally done, they gathered in front of the mausoleum.
It was almost completely destroyed, with only a small entrance leading to a bloody staircase, visibly damaged by the attacks.
The heroes just exchanged glances before cautiously entering the staircase.
It was dark and stuffy. A putrid, sickening smell permeated
everything.
The moment Qingyi's feet stepped at the end of the staircase, he stopped, a strange crack echoing. His boots sank into a strange, brittle
texture.
When he looked down, his eyes widened.
Those were bones. All mortal bones, bearing terrible torture marks.
Looking to the side, he saw cells, hundreds of them, each filled with dozens of frail, broken figures. Their eyes were empty, and their
bodies bore deep signs of torture.
From children to the elderly, and even pregnant women.
No one had been spared.
"W-we need to free them immediately! Celestia exclaimed beside him,
clenching her hands and calling for a silent prayer, immediately
casting a healing spell on those in one of the cells.
To her surprise, there was no relief in their condition; quite the
contrary.
Their lips opened in miserable screams, their bodies writhing as their
eyes widened.
Celestia shuddered, taking a step back and burying her face in
Qingyi's chest.
She did not watch as the bodies exploded.
"Come on, we'll rescue them later..." Lucien said through gritted teeth.
He wasn't angry at the state of those people; quite the contrary.
What made him angry was seeing Celestia like that, clinging to Qingyi
as if he were everything in the world.
Why couldn't it be him?
No... why the hell was this even happening?
Celestia was the Sacred Priestess, she shouldn't be corrupted by
Qingyi's disgusting touch like this!
Lucien's lips parted, almost releasing a protest, before he finally just
looked ahead and nothing but ahead.
He would take care of these things when they returned to the
imperial capital. If Qingyi had truly dared to take Celestia's purity...
Lucien could hardly imagine what would happen, his body trembling
with pleasure.
Yes, that would be a great day!
Soon, the group found themselves walking again, going deeper and
deeper.
They encountered no enemies, only absolute darkness until they finally reached a location.
It was a huge pocket at the lowest part of the cave. The ceiling was
clearly over a kilometer high, while the stony walls seemed to hold firm despite the tens of kilometers separating them.
The place was lit by candles on the floor, revealing tens of thousands
of corpses.
In its center stood a single man.
Tall, with long white hair, blood-red eyes, and a handsome
middle-aged face.
His eyes focused on the heroes who had just arrived, and his Qi
spilled out, along with his mana, falling upon them.
From his back, dozens of tubes connecting his body to a blood reservoir broke, and he smiled.
Qingyi took a step back, feeling his blood burn.
That man was powerful, more powerful than any enemy he had faced
in a long time.

chapters.title: Chapter 465 Now, you just die.
paragraphs: "Don't expose yourselves too much, always stay on the defensive." Qingyi instructed his wives, tightening his grip on the hilt of the Heaven-Defying Thunder Sword.
It would be best to immediately send them to the Mind World and resolve the matter himself. However, Qingyi hesitated.
At his side, Lucien stepped forward, swinging his sword toward the man, his movement too fast for any mortal eye to follow.
The man took a single step forward.
The last three cables that still connected his body to the blood reservoir finally broke away from his back, falling to the ground with a crack and leaking blood nonstop.
The man's feet hit the golden floor, the black holes in his back slowly closing.
He moved his right hand, comically slowly.
Still, the power was terrifying.
Lucien, who was only a few feet away from him, barely had time to react. His head spun so hard that it was almost torn from his neck, a fiery red stain appearing on his face.
Lucien's consciousness wavered, and when he realized it, his back was sinking into the stone, a horrible pain spreading through his neck and back.
In his mind, it all took long seconds, but in reality, it was only a moment, a simple movement of the hands.
A full second passed before the shockwave arrived, the man's long white hair flying with the impact.
His blood-red eyes swept over everyone there. His aged but handsome and virile face revealed a gentle smile.
"Hm... I can see that I have had many wonderful and unexpected guests... their souls will be of good use to me!"
"Retreat now!" Qingyi roared, moving to send them to the Mind World.
He had already given them artifacts capable of sending them there instantly, but he would not blindly trust these items.
Unfortunately, it was already too late.
In a fraction of a breath, the demonic cultist was already in front of Qingyi, his clenched fist flying toward his face.
The handsome young man gritted his teeth, immediately calling upon the Flames of Primordial Chaos.
This time, he would not have the luxury of holding back.
His attacker's eyes, previously cold and full of amusement, suddenly changed, his entire momentum ending in a single moment.
He tried to retreat, but the gray flames had already reached his right
arm.
He formed a blade of Qi with his left arm, his face filling with pain as he cut off his own limb, at the same time as Qingyi's kick met his stomach.
Burning blood fell to the ground as the man retreated dozens of steps, Qingyi's kick knocking the air from his chest.

"Ugh... boy, you have something very profane inside you, huh? Hahaha." The man laughed, holding out his severed arm. In a single moment, another grew in its place. "We should be allies, not enemies, you know?"
Qingyi opened his lips to respond, shocked that this demonic man had been able to regenerate so quickly.
But before he could even say anything, Celestia roared beside him. "Hubby has nothing profane about him, and he would never join
forces with a demon like you! Because he is the prophesied hero of Auranys, Goddess of Light and-"
Celestia didn't finish her sentence, a high-pitched scream escaping her lips as she was pulled into the Mind World.
Sapphire and Aeryn tried to protest, and indeed did protest. Both wanted to stay and fight; they weren't defenseless like Celestia.
But they had also seen how easily Lucien had been defeated and that, even though Qingyi had been able to easily fend off that attack, he didn't have the luxury of fighting while protecting them.
"Hm..." The demonic man spat blood on the ground, feeling his abdomen burn from Qingyi's blow.
That had hurt, really hurt.
"You know... you never cease to amaze me. Even a Mind World?"
Qingyi shuddered at those words. How the hell did that man identify a Mind World? He wasn't from the Celestial Heaven, was he?
"Fucking the pussies of the three heroines chosen by the church of Auranys and even storing them in the Mind World...

You know, I originally planned to use all of your souls to feed the creation of a vessel for my Lord. I may have to pull them out of this Mind World in order to use them, but I believe only your soul will be
necessary, hahaha."
Qingyi ignored most of that man's words, focusing only on what
mattered to him.
"And you're going to tell me who this Lord is?" He asked, watching the
demonic man coldly.
As he expected, there was something else.
Not only did they know that the five heroes were coming there, but
they were even making themselves vulnerable to facilitate that
encounter.
There was someone inside the church, someone with great influence
who served whoever this "Lord" was.
If Qingyi weren't here, he was sure: everyone would die.
Who could it be? Perhaps the bishop who sent them there?
His haste was indeed suspicious. However, Qingyi was unable to be
sure now.
"Oh... you will know his name. You will know it as soon as your soul is
swallowed by him, as soon as you have the honor of one day being part of something greater than your pathetic little existence, the chance to serve something greater!"
The man opened his arms, his voice full of fanaticism.
Suddenly, he fell silent, his eyes falling on Qingyi, cold and cruel.
"But not now. Now, you just die."
Without them realizing it, someone was listening to their
conversation.
Qingyi couldn't give a damn about what happened to Lucien and, at
that very moment, was focusing only on the enemy in front of him.

But Lucien could hear him very well and also heard very well what Celestia said before being sent to the World of the Mind. 'Qingyi was the prophesied hero for Auranys... Lucien repeated in his mind, over and over again.
WHAT THE HELL DID THAT WOMAN MEAN BY THAT?
He was the prophesied hero, not Qingyi. From the day he arrived in
this world, he knew that.
It was on his Status Screen, how could the System lie to him?
It was impossible, he knew it was!
Lucien gritted his teeth, his heart filling with nothing but pure rage
and jealousy.

chapters.title: Chapter 466 - I prefer to call you a filthy cuckold, just like your master.
paragraphs: "Tell me your name," Qingyi demanded, continuing to stare at the demonic cultist.
Neither of them paid any attention to the worm wriggling beside them.
"You can call me Mo Xuetian, or the Blood Knight," the man said, his face full of amusement.
"Hm... I prefer to call you a filthy cuckold, just like your master."
To Qingyi's surprise, the moment he heard those words, Xuetian did not respond with anger.
Quite the contrary, his lips parted in a loud, booming laugh.
"I appreciate your courage, young man." Xuetian stretched. "Although it will bring about your end far too soon."
The moment Xuetian's voice fell, he disappeared. His body turned into a blur, reappearing beside Qingyi and punching with all his might.
The two fists met with a crash, right in the center of that place.

The throne Xuetian sat on was the first thing to be destroyed as the shockwave spread. The hard stone beneath his feet was turned to dust, and the bones were pushed into the rocky walls in the corner. The demonic cultist couldn't hide the surprise on his face as he was forced to take exactly two steps back. Qingyi, however, took only one.
He believed that Qingyi was, at most, slightly weaker than him. But that one contact was enough for him to be certain.
Physically, Qingyi was stronger than him.
That brought a drop of uncertainty to the man's face.
He hated uncertainty, but he also felt curiosity.
How powerful would he become after devouring Qingyi?
In the end, his master only needed the souls.
Gritting his teeth, he extended a single hand. A long, powerful blade of blood formed from a small cut on his wrist.
His lips curled into a smile so wide that the corners of his mouth seemed about to tear, a crazed and greedy light shining in them.
Qingyi drew the Heaven-Defying Thunder Sword, watching the first bloody slashes arrive and a figure appear behind the man.
He couldn't pay attention to this figure as he used the Third Form of the Thunderous Sword Art, breaking Xuetian's attack.
Spinning his body, he threw a flaming spear toward the demonic
cultist.
A powerful explosion echoed as Xuetian tried to parry the spear sent toward him, only to be swallowed by a sea of flames.
When the smoke from the explosion cleared and Qingyi could see the figure formed by Xuetian's Bloodline Projection, he was unable to stop his eyes from widening.
Tall, with horns black as night, a powerful body, and gray skin.
Qingyi knew that Bloodline Projection well, very well.
That was the Bloodline Projection of the Celestial Demon, the same demon whose bloodline blessed the Mortal Heaven Demon Cult!
"You have the bloodline of the Celestial Demon?!" Qingyi questioned, gritting his teeth and also calling upon his own Bloodline Projection.
Immediately, a black dragon appeared behind him, the stone walls shaking as its roar echoed.
Fortunately, that place was more than large enough to fit him at full strength.
"The dead don't need to know this kind of thing." Xuetian growled, preparing his blade again. His mood soured as he felt his skin burn with those cursed flames.
'Why the hell is it so hot? How high could the affinity with fire of this... this... disgusting worm be?' Xuetian wondered, watching the black dragon behind Qingyi.
He could feel his bloodline trembling, his cultivation being suppressed, and it only filled him with even more rage.
How dare that bastard make the gift he received from his Lord tremble?
Xuetian readied his blade again and then charged forward.
Qingyi did the same. In the center of it all, the two blades clashed.
A sea of blood and thunder Qi aura engulfed everything around them, the entire cave and even the forest above being taken over by violent tremors.
The two stared at each other for a moment, the air boiling from the standoff between their Qis. Every drop of blood surrounding them was immediately turned to vapor.
Qingyi could feel his muscles burning.

For the first time in a long time, he had that feeling: the feeling of pushing against a wall, of putting all his strength into his muscles and not feeling the enemy immediately collapse under the pressure.
That wasn't bad at all.
With a thrust of his feet, he pushed Xuetian away and then attacked.
Their blades met dozens of times in a single second, the explosions consuming everything in front of them.
Above them, the entire cave began to collapse, but that didn't matter.
Any rock that even came close to them was immediately turned to dust, both above and below.
Just one more clash of blades later, and the sun was already bathing
their bodies. Their weapons sparkled as they met again and again. The new opening revealed a crater more than ten kilometers long and nearly two kilometers deep.
"I think it's time to end this, young man!" Xuetian roared, appearing in one of the corners.
His body was covered in small wounds, his right eye gouged out, his skull broken, and his left leg held in place by only a small piece of skin.
Qingyi wasn't much better either. A gash ran from his chest to his abdomen; his left hand had been completely torn off, while his right hand bled profusely.

His hands closed tightly around the hilt of his sword, preventing it from escaping his grip as the Seed of Life slowly healed him. "Yes, it must be the best." Qingyi spoke coldly, moving his Shadow Qi as his enemy ascended to the skies.
Crimson wings of blood appeared on Xuetian's back, his bloody sword transforming into a spear.
Qingyi closed his eyes, calling upon his Shadow Qi, feeling all the Qi around him being sucked toward him, the deep shadows devouring
everything.
He took a deep breath. He inhaled and then attacked, using the Ten Thousand Shadows Devouring Art, noticing Xuetian's figure rapidly
approaching.
But then, at the last moment, the second before the attacks met, Qingyi felt something; a deep pain in his ribs.
"Die, you bastard!" Lucien roared with nothing but the deepest
hatred.

paragraphs: "Ugh... damn it, this will be deducted from your pay!" The old man yelled at Lucas.
The young man just turned his face away. His father had forced him to work there, but he hadn't taken his fortune away.
He couldn't give a damn about that old man's miserable pay.
Under the old man's angry gaze, he just returned to his dragon, who was watching Qingyi with eyes full of suspicion and contempt.
"Like mount, like rider." Qingyi shook his head, focusing on the old
man.
"I am a traveler and wish to purchase a ticket to the capital, DragonPeak," Qingyi said, watching the old man's face change immediately.
His grumpy expression faded, replaced by a big, bright smile.
"Oh... perfect, dear customer! Come with me, come! We have a carriage about to leave! Hehehe."
The old man grabbed Qingyi's arm, leading him into his simple office. There, Qingyi paid, signed some documents, and then waited.
He could even go alone.
With his speed and affinity for space and darkness, he would likely arrive in the capital unscathed. Getting through their defensive and detection formations shouldn't be too difficult either.
Still, he preferred to take the more traditional route, taking the time to discover as much as he could about that land.
After all, even Aeryn had never been there.
All the elven beauty knew about those people came from ancient books, books that always portrayed them as traitors to the elven
people and which were clearly full of political propaganda.
The same was true for Sapphire, whose people also hated the Grand Duchy of Vaeldrinn.
'I just hope they're not all assholes like this guy... Qingyi flashed a bitter smile, feeling Lucas's burning gaze on his back.
What had he done to deserve the hatred of such a pathetic little creature?
Qingyi continued to ignore him until, finally, his companions arrived.
They were all men, identifiable as miners by their clothes and equipment. Their faces were tired, and their eyes met Lucas's for a brief moment before dropping to the ground.
If it weren't for the extremely low price, no one there would choose that old man's escort. Not while Lucas was present.
They had even seen one of their companions devoured by that cursed beast before.
"All right, get in the carriage! Let's start the journey as soon as possible, I want you to get there before the rise of the RedDeath!" The old man said, slapping the coachman on the back.
Honestly, calling it a carriage was an exaggeration. It was little better than an ordinary freight wagon, with rags used for cover.
Without even giving Qingyi or the miners in the wagon a second glance, Lucas rose into the skies, flying away with his beast.
"What is the RedDeath?" Qingyi asked, sitting among the miners, who relaxed as soon as Lucas left.
"Oh... you're a foreigner, right?" One of the miners asked, observing Qingyi's unique features and strange clothes.
Black robes, decorated with strange golden flying serpents.
Qingyi was clearly a very wealthy nobleman. What the hell was he doing among them, the rabble of the rabble?
"Yes, I am from a distant land," Qingyi replied, receiving nods of understanding from the men.

"RedDeath is the Patriarch's dragon. He recently reached over eighty meters in height, and the Patriarch wishes to deliver Karlan's heart to him. They say that, in doing so, he may even attain the power of Khaedryss!"
The miner spoke, his eyes shining as he imagined such a beast.
They had been ruled by the draconic elves for tens of thousands of years, for countless mortal generations.
Therefore, the humans there already saw those people as their legitimate rulers and, above all, as gods who ruled the skies.
"Hm..." Qingyi scratched his chin.
Aeryn had spoken of a certain Karlan, one of the two dragons who helped lay the foundation for the existence of the draconic elves.
Karlan, the female, had been dead for a long time, while the condition
of the male ancestor was not even known.
Some said he had died a few thousand years ago; others said he had isolated himself after the death of his partner.
But that mattered little to the common people. Khaedryss had not appeared in public for many decades.
For the common people, the birth of another beast like her was a great blessing for the entire Grand Duchy of Vaeldrinn.
Shaking his head, Qingyi focused solely on the journey.
From what the miners had said, it would take at least a few weeks to
reach the capital, with the RedDeath's ascension taking place in a
month or two.
'Hmm... would it be too greedy to try to take that from them too?" Qingyi wondered.
The only way for the Red Death to consume Karlan's heart was through a long and complicated ritual, but the same was not true for
Khaedryss.
She could just devour it freely and absorb its power.
Currently, she was already powerful enough to kill an immortal
emperor, and Qingyi was certain: just a little more, a few good corpses, and he would see Khaedryss at her peak of power again.

Now, they had entered a strange forest.
Each tree was identical and vast, rising over fifty meters high, with branches only at the top.
Their trunks were completely smooth, white, and perfect, planted so densely that Qingyi could barely see beyond a few dozen meters ahead without using his draconic eyes.
Qingyi was about to ask the miners about this forest, but suddenly fell
silent.
His senses screamed in alert and his hand flowed to the hilt of the
Heaven-Defying Thunder Sword.
His eyes rose and he saw Lucas' dragon also become agitated.
Something was chasing them.
Heavy footsteps echoed in the distance. Dozens, no... hundreds of
them.
Whatever was approaching was large. And from the murderous intent
Qingyi could sense, it was hungry.
"Oh, what are you doing, young man?" One of the miners asked.
He was only a mortal and couldn't sense the same thing Qingyi or
Lucas could, so he couldn't help but be surprised when the handsome young man suddenly stood up.
"Get ready to hide," Qingyi growled, the Heaven-Defying Thunder
Sword sliding out of its sheath.

sentences.text: "Ugh... damn it, this will be deducted from your pay!" The old man yelled at Lucas.
The young man just turned his face away.
His father had forced him to work there, but he hadn't taken his fortune away.
He couldn't give a damn about that old man's miserable pay.
Under the old man's angry gaze, he just returned to his dragon, who was watching Qingyi with eyes full of suspicion and contempt.
"Like mount, like rider." Qingyi shook his head, focusing on the old
man.
"I am a traveler and wish to purchase a ticket to the capital, DragonPeak," Qingyi said, watching the old man's face change immediately.
His grumpy expression faded, replaced by a big, bright smile.
"Oh... perfect, dear customer!
Come with me, come!
We have a carriage about to leave!
Hehehe."
The old man grabbed Qingyi's arm, leading him into his simple office.
There, Qingyi paid, signed some documents, and then waited.
He could even go alone.
With his speed and affinity for space and darkness, he would likely arrive in the capital unscathed.
Getting through their defensive and detection formations shouldn't be too difficult either.
Still, he preferred to take the more traditional route, taking the time to discover as much as he could about that land.
After all, even Aeryn had never been there.
All the elven beauty knew about those people came from ancient books, books that always portrayed them as traitors to the elven
people and which were clearly full of political propaganda.
The same was true for Sapphire, whose people also hated the Grand Duchy of Vaeldrinn.
'I just hope they're not all assholes like this guy...
Qingyi flashed a bitter smile, feeling Lucas's burning gaze on his back.
What had he done to deserve the hatred of such a pathetic little creature?

Their faces were tired, and their eyes met Lucas's for a brief moment before dropping to the ground.
If it weren't for the extremely low price, no one there would choose that old man's escort.
Not while Lucas was present.
They had even seen one of their companions devoured by that cursed beast before.
"All right, get in the carriage!

It was little better than an ordinary freight wagon, with rags used for cover.

chapters.title: Chapter 475 - You could have had a long life
paragraphs: The first of the creatures appeared: a giant wind-horned wolf.
It was barely three meters long, but its power in a pack was something even Lucas couldn't ignore.
Of course, to Qingyi, it wasn't much.
They were just insignificant base predators looking for easy prey, the most powerful of them barely reaching the level of a false immortal.
Qingyi jumped out of the carriage, ready to cut down the first ten in front of him.
Unfortunately, he had to stop at the last second.
His feet sank into the muddy ground and an intense heat rose up behind him, rapidly approaching.
It was Lucas's dragon.
Its huge mouth was open while its master flashed a sadistic smile, orange, burning flames falling onto the ground.
This was no accident; Lucas was aiming at Qingyi.
Qingyi just formed a Qi barrier around himself, realizing that the beasts were already surrounding the carriage.
With a single movement of his eyes, his body disappeared.
When he reappeared, he was already above the carriage, exactly ten blades of Qi leaving his body and falling on the wolves.
Groans and growls full of agony echoed as severed paws, tails, and canine heads fell to the ground.
Just ahead, Lucas's dragon's flame swallowed more than half of the pack.
"Ugh... better get rid of these damn things first," Qingyi whispered irritably, as his body was swallowed by another spatial fold.
He didn't truly care about the death of those miners, but if he could defend them without losing anything in return, why wouldn't he?
The lives of those who were not his enemies were worth more than a minor inconvenience to him.
In a single second, he appeared beside the remaining wolves.
Flying blades cut through flesh with ease, exterminating them as if they were nothing more than ants.
When the last one fell to the ground, Qingyi couldn't help but smile with satisfaction, lazily cracking his neck.
He had shown more power than he wanted to and, most certainly, than was necessary.
But for him, what mattered most was that he had gotten a good warm-up.
He turned toward the miners, just in time to see, with his guard down, the flames of Lucas's dragon engulfing them as the beast tore through the air.
"Die, you bastard!" Lucas roared, not caring about the consequences.
They were just a few random commoners.
As long as there were no witnesses, nothing had happened, right? A smile full of amusement dominated his sadistic face as his dragon landed, unleashing its flames toward Qingyi without stopping.
Neither of them noticed that, during all this, Qingyi was completely still.
His expression was relaxed, and only a thin layer of Qi protected his clothes as he was engulfed by the flames.
"Hm... this is a very pleasant sauna..." Qingyi grunted, an annoyed smile taking over his handsome masculine face.
"Khaedryss, how about an extra hearty meal today?"
"Uh?" Lucas's eyes widened upon hearing those words.
He barely paid attention to what was said, shocked only by the fact that Qingyi was alive.
By the time he finally had the capacity to realize what was happening, it was already too late.
His dragon turned, taking to the skies with desperate flaps of its
wings.
Where its flames fell, a thick veil of white smoke and steam from the muddy ground began to rise, hiding Qingyi within.
"What are you doing? Stay and fight!" Lucas shouted, slapping his dragon's neck.
He didn't even notice when the white smoke covering Qingyi parted with a bang, black scales like the night glistening in the sunlight.
A jaw, so large that Lucas's dragon was barely enough to fill it, opened.
A powerful, armored neck stretched out as endless rows of sharp teeth closed around Lucas and his mount.
Only then did Lucas feel the pain, a pain he had never felt in his entire life.
As he lost feeling in his legs and was thrown away, still clinging to his mount's head, he understood why his mount was fleeing.
Behind him was a huge beast, one he only recognized from statues and stories of past glory.
The creature's roar caused extreme terror in the young elf's eyes.
Khaedryss barely paid attention to Lucas, voraciously devouring his
dragon.
When she was finished, she lowered her head, her jaw opening to let
out a long, angry growl.
"You know, brat..." Qingyi jumped on top of Khaedryss's head,
watching Lucas.
There was no more arrogance on his face, and his legs had been replaced by nothing but a bloody mess, devoured by the black dragon.
"You could have had a long life, enjoying your family's countless riches, fucking beautiful whores, and drinking fine wine," Qingyi said.
Khaedryss's lips parted, revealing sharp teeth, and a strange black light emerged from the depths of her throat.
Lucas despaired, his pants dampening with urine as he screamed and
begged.
For the first time in his entire life, he was in mortal danger. Real
mortal danger.
Unfortunately for him, Khaedryss did not listen to pleas.
Her flames engulfed everything: clothes, weapons, even the
decapitated head of his mount.
Everything was vaporized into nothing but ashes by the flames of the
butcher of empires and slayer of immortals.
When she was done, Khaedryss raised her face and then opened her
jaws.
Her thunderous roar echoed for countless kilometers, the
surrounding forest shaking.
She could taste that air, taste that blood, one she hadn't tasted in
many, many years.
She was back home.
"Good girl..." Qingyi smiled, patting Khaedryss on the neck.
She had more than doubled in size compared to when he first found
her, reaching ninety meters in length and weighing close to a hundred tons.
It was even a little comical for Qingyi, so small in comparison to her,
to stroke her scales.
Still, she enjoyed it, feeling the warm, affectionate touch of her rider.
"Return to the world of the mind. Soon the time will come for you to bathe in the blood of your enemies and devour Karlan's heart."

As he spoke those last words, Qingyi noticed a unique excitement take hold of Khaedryss's face, one that he found strangely amusing. Apparently, she was also excited about the idea of eating Karlan's heart.

chapters.title: Chapter 476 The worst!
paragraphs: Qingyi looked at the corpses incinerated by Lucas' dragon flames.
He could have saved them, for sure.
With a single moment, a fraction of a fraction of a second. That was all it took to save them.
Still, he didn't. He failed to save them. If he had kept his guard up, none of this would have happened...
Qingyi shifted his attention, lowered his guard.
To Qingyi, Lucas had no reason to focus on those miners, not when he could just focus on the person on whom all his hatred was concentrated.
What was the point of killing them too?
"Ah... I forgot..." Qingyi sighed heavily.
He had forgotten that in this world, some people were evil just because they were.
They killed because they could, nothing more.
Qingyi didn't think much about it, knowing it would be useless. He reached the corpses, clasped his fists, and then said: "May the heavens take care of their souls."
With nothing else to do, Qingyi left, his body exploding with speed.
On one hand, many of his plans had been ruined; on the other, at least he would get there faster.
Shaking his head, he quickened his pace, a sea of shadows engulfing his body as his speed increased dramatically.
He was much faster than the speed of sound. However, there was no shockwave or sonic boom, his shadow Qi causing him to barely affect the world around him.
Any mortal eye would be unable to keep up with such speed, but for Qingyi, even traveling through those dense trees was easy.
The journey that would have taken weeks by carriage, he made in less than an hour.
He felt many beasts probing him as he traveled, some even capable of posing a danger to his life, but he ignored everything and only stopped when he sensed a great change in the mana around him.
The density skyrocketed to an absurd level, his fingers tingling as he inhaled, feeling the air fill his lungs.
Pure and perfect, second only to the air of the world of the mind.
With light steps, Qingyi began to walk slowly until he reached a wide central road, surrounded by well-kept trees, the road itself meticulously covered with stones in beautiful patterns.
Thousands of merchants and travelers took this road, so it wasn't difficult to blend in, even with his unique appearance.
He didn't bother to hide either.
No one there knew his face, after all.
He continued for a brief moment before, just after a small hill, suddenly stopping, his eyes scanning the city ahead.
It was just over ten kilometers away, surrounded by a huge wall from which large chains rose toward the skies.

These chains were tied to a huge flying island, a mass of land held together by such an absurd amount of mana that Qingyi was sure that even with all the riches accumulated alongside Meilin, he would not be able to maintain it for more than a few days.
His eyes scanned the many fortresses that rose above that island, like deities over the city.
That was the place he needed to reach to find Elize's sister.
[Husband... I know this place. It's a little faded in my memory, but I'm
sure I've been here before.]
Elize's voice echoed as she watched everything through Ruxue's eyes.
This was the place where she had spent her childhood until her mother's death.
"Just wait a little longer, love. Qingyi whispered to her, continuing to walk.
At the central gates, a group of guards watched the crowd with attentive eyes, collecting travelers' documents and collective
transportation permits.
Despite the high guard, they barely noticed when Qingyi's body was swallowed by a dark blur, disappearing before appearing on the other side of the gate.
Many guards turned their faces in confusion, spreading their senses of mana.
They felt as if something had just passed them by, but they had no idea what it was, nor whether their senses were simply deceiving
them.
In the end, they just exchanged glances and continued their service. "It's... pleasant." Qingyi murmured after walking for a moment.
Not just the air, nor the silence, nor the nature.
Everything there was pleasant, from the architecture to the children
playing in the street.
Qingyi's eyes soon followed those of the children, focusing on the skies, where two dragon riders were having a friendly duel,
exchanging bursts of flames.
The children shouted with excitement at the beautiful sight, while
the adults looked on with reverence.
He could already imagine that many of these children dreamed of one day becoming dragon riders themselves.
Unfortunately, such a dream was almost impossible.
At the end of the day, they were just mortal humans and would hardly
be anything more than that.
Qingyi shook his head and continued on his way.
They weren't the first and wouldn't be the last.
He was about to start looking for a tavern to listen to rumors when he
felt a pair of small hands tugging at his robes.
"Oh... handsome uncle! Do you want to get to the huge black castle
too?"
Turning around, Qingyi saw a little girl with short brown hair and large amber eyes, watching him with interest and sparkle.
Judging by her clothes, she was probably a child from a middle-class
family.
"Yes," Qingyi nodded, flashing a gentle smile. "Didn't your parents teach you not to talk to strangers on the street?"
"Oh... are you a bad man?" The little girl took a step back, her eyes
fluttering.
[The worst!] Ruxue's voice echoed in Qingyi's mind, whose smile expanded even further, ignoring his wife's words.
"To my enemies, yes, I am a bad man."
"Oh... cool!" The little girl's eyes sparkled. "Daddy always said that if
we wanted to go to the big black castle, we had to be next to a
pureblood, a real one!"
'Pureblood?' Qingyi wondered.
Was she talking about dragon riders?
He already knew that, despite limitations, humans could also become
riders.
But was there a separation between human riders and elven riders?
[When a human becomes a dragon rider, their constitution tends to change to adapt to this new power.
That must be what she's talking about, any common elven rider or a
human rider whose constitution has already fully adapted to their
mount.]
It was Aeryn who answered that question, also using his connection with Ruxue.

DragonPeak, the capital of the dragon people, was divided into three parts.
The first was the outer region.
There was no division between the poor and the middle class here, as poverty had been virtually
eradicated throughout the capital.
The second was the noble region, inhabited by human nobles, wealthy merchants, and large corporations.
The only access without passing through the detection arrays that protected the flying island from intruders was in the noble region.

The third region, of course, was the flying island itself, known as the cloud region or simply as the black castle, referring to the residence of the patriarch and the high nobility of the draconic elves.
This access was a huge teleportation platform, always guarded by a thousand guards, each of whom was at least a true immortal.
On this particular day, however, there were many more guards, carefully controlling the crowd as an arena was prepared in a huge square in front of the platform.

For each banner, there was a throne, each throne serving as a seat for
a powerful expert.

Instead of someone sitting on the throne, there was a woman fully protected with powerful black steel armor.

families!

chapters.title: Chapter 480 Lucios
paragraphs: The Bronze Dragon hovered elegantly, its emerald green eyes scanning the crowd.
It did not flap its wings, keeping them open at their full wingspan of over one hundred and thirty meters, its shadow engulfing everything below.
His rider's armor glistened in gold, emanating an aura superior even to that of the beast he rode.
Only a fraction of it was released, and half of the competitors fell to the ground.
A second wave of pressure, and the thousands were reduced to little more than a hundred.
The powerful expert barely paid attention to those who fell, merely waving his hand.
The bodies of the unconscious were swept toward the wide streets, where healers promptly took them away for treatment.
"Very good." His voice echoed, old yet noble and full of vitality.
He counted the remnants; about one hundred and thirty, of which only fifty would be chosen.
Obviously, even among these fifty, not all would become dragon riders.
If only five succeeded, it would already be a resounding selection.
After thinking for a moment, the old man carefully released his aura, knocking down two more and setting the number at one hundred and twenty-eight.
"I am Lucios Vaeldrinn Valerio, patriarch of House Valerio. Many here must already know my name." The expert spoke, eliciting sighs from the crowd.
Lucios was renowned in the capital, being one of the experts who worked side by side with the first ancestor of the draconic elves and founded the Grand Duchy of Vaeldrinn.
After Khaedryss at her peak and the founding dragon couple, he was probably the most powerful and respected being in the entire land of the draconic elves. An expert of the twelfth ring.
Even Qingyi knew him, especially because of one specific fact: Lucios was primarily responsible for the current patriarch remaining in power.
If the old man stood in the way, Qingyi knew that with his current power, it would be basically impossible to avenge Elize's mother.
"Hm..." Qingyi scratched his chin, thinking for a brief moment before focusing on the powerful expert.
"We have one hundred and twenty-eight here. You will fight, and the fifty most powerful will be selected. I myself will take one as my champion."
The murmurs among the young people became even more uncontrolled, expressions full of excitement spreading across their faces.

"Hm... I wonder if I should reduce the number to sixty-four..." Old Lucios stroked his gray beard, and immediately the murmurs ceased. With a smile, he simply waved his hands, and the double doors of the arena opened, allowing the participants to enter.
There was no special place for them to sit, not even an audience, except for the experts seated on the many thrones surrounding the
venue.
It was just a simple, small concrete platform, no more than a thousand square meters.
At least on the outside.
As he walked across the concrete platform, Qingyi felt the power of
the spatial barriers that held it together and would contain the battle.
It took him only a moment to be sure: even for him, it would be difficult to destroy it easily.
Old Lucios sat on the throne next to the one reserved for the patriarch, ignoring the surprised looks of the other leaders of internal factions and large families.
"Very well, the first pair may come up." Lucios spoke, waving his hand as two flashes of light fell on two of the young people.
With a moment's hesitation, they stepped forward, standing face to
face and waiting for the expert's confirmation.
The moment Lucios' hand touched the arm of his seat, the two
stepped forward without holding back.
Unlike what elves usually preferred, this was not a test full of rules,
rituals, and parameters to be achieved. Quite the contrary.
This was simply a demonstration of strength and power.
In the end, that is what dragons represent.
From Khaedryss to the bronze beast flying above the arena. Every dragon, with a few exceptions, was the embodiment of violence, destruction, and arrogance, their wisdom being just one more aspect.
Perhaps that was the biggest difference between the so-called draconic elves and their cousins.
And in that way, those young men fought, their swords meeting in the center of the arena with a thunderous explosion.
Their powers, equivalent to those of a True Immortal, caused destruction all around them.
They separated for a moment before advancing again, their bodies covered in crimson auras, a strange kind of flaming mana surrounding
them.
Many had to take a step back immediately, protecting themselves
with thin mana barriers as the scorching heat hit their faces.
Only Qingyi and a few others remained completely unmoved.
Honestly, the handsome young man was more interested in the strength of that concrete than anything else.
After all, it was difficult for him to find an arena where he could train without completely and immediately destroying it.
The combat didn't have many other peak moments after the initial clash. Dozens of exchanges of blows took over the arena until, finally, the younger man gave in.
His opponent's blade slid down his own to the hilt before, with an
explosion of mana, disarming him, taking a few fingers with it.
When the younger man fell on his butt on the floor, grunting and holding his bloody hand, the older man raised his sword with a roar of
victory.
He had won and, unlike his opponent, had not suffered a single injury.
With a big smile, he stepped down from the arena and sat in a corner, immediately beginning to rest.
The wounded man was removed from the arena, the blood cleaned from the floor, and then Lucios stood up again.
Despite the intense combat, the old expert still looked bored, his eyes scanning the young men until they fell on two in particular.
One of them was, to his surprise, a pureblood of his race. He had long golden hair, tenth ring power, and a beautiful, calm face.
A pureblood by birth who did not belong to any great family.
The other was a young man who made him even more curious. He was clearly human, despite having a scent that did not belong to a
human and an absurd amount of hidden power, something that shocked even him.
How did a human body not explode with all that stored energy?

chapters.title: Chapter 481 Insolent brat!
paragraphs: The more Lucios watched the two, the more his thin, old lips curved, a huge smile taking over his wrinkled face.
He waved his hands, and then two orbs of light hovered over the two young men.
Qingyi observed his opponent with interest before climbing into the arena, cracking his knuckles and holding the Heaven-Defying Thunder Sword firmly.
"You have a beautiful sword, stranger. My name is Lux, what is yours?" The young man asked, extending his hand.
"Qingyi." Qingyi replied briefly and coldly, accepting Lux's handshake.
The moment he extended his hand, however, he sensed danger.
His left foot sank slightly into the ground, his vision blurring as he changed direction in the blink of an eye.
At the same time, the saber Lux carried at his waist became nothing more than a golden blur, his right hand moving at an absurd speed.
A sharp crack echoed, and then a powerful slash tore the arena in half, missing Qingyi by inches.
"Oh... that's powerful, at least for an ant." Qingyi smiled disdainfully, watching Lux's shocked face.
Turning his body, the handsome young man kicked out, his boots hitting Lux's face with a thud and sending him crashing into the barrier.
"Ugh... son of a bitch." Lux groaned painfully as he fell to his knees, coughing up blood and a few broken teeth onto the floor.
His nose was red, clearly broken.
"This is going to be interesting, hehehe..." Old Lucios laughed, the long, sharp nail of his index finger tapping against the black steel of
his throne.
Lux took only a single moment before recovering, clutching his chest and then roaring.
"You're fast, but don't think speed alone will be enough, foreign pig!" Lux punched the ground, his body exploding with a golden aura, any sign of humility on his face replaced by pure arrogance.
In the blink of an eye, he covered the distance between him and Qingyi.
His blade struck the Heaven-Defying Thunder Sword with a powerful crash, his roar growing even louder as he pressed harder and harder.
Qingyi grunted softly as his feet tore into the concrete floor, holding back Lux's powerful momentum.
He wasn't even bothered to use his Qi, relying solely on his mana and physical strength.
That was enough to deal with that insect.
Around the two of them, gravity seemed to briefly reverse, small stones from the destroyed arena flying into the air.
Qingyi's lightning-covered mana and Lux's golden Qi carved deep grooves into the concrete.
"Yield!" Lux roared, giving himself another burst of power as he prepared a spell in his left hand, one of the few he had mastered.
"I'm sorry, but I've seen enough." Qingyi finally pushed back with full force, planting his foot on the ground and then moving his sword, thunder, and fire toward his opponent's blade.
In a single moment, steel sank into steel and molten metal fell to the ground.
Lux's eyes widened as Qingyi's sword passed through his and the weight in his hands grew lighter.
Before he was even able to react, Qingyi's fist was already tearing through the air toward his face, covered in a powerful flaming aura.
Many closed their eyes at the thunderous sound of Qingyi's fist landing.
Lux's body spun in the air, his feet hitting the ground before he was violently thrown against the protective barrier.
Under Qingyi's feet, everything turned to dust, and the arrays
surrounding them shook violently.
Even though they were able to contain most of the power shock of an Immortal Emperor like Qingyi, they still couldn't contain it all, and
small cracks spread across the ground.
Mixed reactions took over the faces of all the spectators.
Many family and faction leaders stood up from their thrones, looking
at that young man with endless greed.
They wanted to take him as their champion right now, brainwash him,
train him, and turn him into an unmatched blade against their
enemies.
But none of them dared to say anything, waiting for old Lucios'
reaction.
The guard sent by Seraphine, Viola, was no different, although now her mind was focused on something else.
'A man who doesn't seem to be of this world... Viola repeated in her mind, her eyes focusing on Lux.
For a moment, she thought it was because of his beauty, but seeing him like that, with his jaw broken and his face turned into a bloody mess, made her dismiss this thought.
Her young lady would never pay attention to someone like that.
So Viola focused on Qingyi.
Much more handsome than Lux, with strange clothes, strange habits,
and even a strange way of walking.
Still, accompanying him was extreme power.
"Boy..." Lucios' voice echoed, snapping Viola out of her stupor.
"I was only looking for a champion, a warrior who would serve my
family forever and who would one day ride a dragon by my side." Lucios rose from his throne, puffing out his chest.
Usually, they would only begin choosing their champions after the
last battle; those were the rules.
But he couldn't give a fuck about the rules.
Among the draconic elves, even the patriarch obeyed him.
The other eleven great families trembled at his power.
"But I've changed my mind, become my apprentice-no, my godson! If
you want, I'll even marry you to one of my granddaughters and make you my heir!" Lucios roared, opening his arms as if to pull Qingyi into
an embrace.
Those words caused even more shock among the thrones, but no one dared to say anything.
Qingyi thought for a moment, scratched his chin, and then shook his
head.
The smile on Lucios' face disappeared, but he didn't care.
"I beg your pardon, senior, but this junior came here with the sole
intention of serving Lady Seraphine. I will not accept any invitation that does not come from her faction."
The shock caused by Lucios' words was incomparable to the shock
caused by Qingyi's refusal.
"What an insolent brat!"
"How dare you refuse Lord Lucios?"
"Do you know who you're talking to?"
Qingyi ignored everyone, his eyes focused only on Viola.
